beats.vo: Hello, champ! Welcome back to Mentr Learn. I am so happy you are here today.
beats.caption: Hello, champ! Welcome to class

beats.vo: Today we start Computer Science — Unit one — How Computers Work.
beats.caption: Unit 1 · How Computers Work

beats.vo: This is Chapter one. The name of our lesson is: What Is a Computer?
beats.caption: Chapter 1 · What Is a Computer?

beats.vo: Say the title with me, nice and slow… What… Is… A… Computer?
beats.caption: Say with me: What Is a Computer?

beats.vo: Great! Keep that title in your mind. Ready? Let's go.
beats.caption: Great! Let's begin

beats.vo: Look around your home. Phones, TVs, fans, toasters, lamps… so many machines!
beats.caption: So many machines at home…

beats.vo: But wait. Are all of them computers? Hmm. What do you think?
beats.caption: Are ALL of them computers?

beats.vo: Pause and think for a moment. Point to one thing near you that you think is a computer.
beats.caption: ⏸ Your turn — point to a computer!

beats.vo: Good thinking! We will check your answer together at the end.
beats.caption: Good thinking! We'll check soon

beats.vo: Here is the big secret. A computer is a special machine with three jobs.
beats.caption: Secret: a computer has 3 jobs

beats.vo: Job one — INPUT. That means something goes in.
beats.caption: 1 · INPUT = something goes in

beats.vo: Job two — PROCESS. That means the machine thinks, or works on it.
beats.caption: 2 · PROCESS = it thinks / works

beats.vo: Job three — OUTPUT. That means something comes out — an answer, a picture, or a sound.
beats.caption: 3 · OUTPUT = something comes out

beats.vo: Let's say the three jobs together: Input… Process… Output!
beats.caption: Say together: Input · Process · Output

beats.vo: Wonderful. If a machine does all three jobs, we can call it a computer.
beats.caption: All 3 jobs → it's a computer

beats.vo: Let's try a real story. Imagine you send a message to your friend on a phone.
beats.caption: Story: sending a message

beats.vo: First, you type the words with your fingers. That is INPUT — words going in.
beats.caption: You type → INPUT

beats.vo: Next, the phone works on your message — it gets it ready to send. That is PROCESS.
beats.caption: Phone works → PROCESS

beats.vo: Then your friend sees the message on their screen. That is OUTPUT.
beats.caption: Friend sees it → OUTPUT

beats.vo: So — input, process, output. Your phone did all three jobs. Your phone is a computer!
beats.caption: Phone = computer ✓

beats.vo: A laptop can do the same. A tablet can do the same. They are computers too.
beats.caption: Laptop · Phone · Tablet = computers

beats.vo: Now, another story. You press a switch, and a bulb lights up.
beats.caption: Story: switching on a bulb

beats.vo: The switch sends power. The bulb gets hot and shines. That is useful!
beats.caption: Useful — but is it a computer?

beats.vo: But the bulb is not taking many kinds of input and thinking about a message or a game.
beats.caption: No real “thinking” like a computer

beats.vo: It mainly turns light on or off. So a simple bulb — or a toaster that only heats bread — is not a computer.
beats.caption: Bulb · Toaster → NOT computers

beats.vo: Remember: computers take input, process it, and show output in a smarter way.
beats.caption: Computers work in a smarter way

beats.vo: Quick game time! I will name something. You say YES if it is a computer, or NO if it is not.
beats.caption: Game: say YES or NO!

beats.vo: Ready? Laptop… Yes! A laptop is a computer.
beats.caption: Laptop → YES ✓

beats.vo: Phone… Yes! A phone is a computer.
beats.caption: Phone → YES ✓

beats.vo: Tablet… Yes! A tablet is a computer.
beats.caption: Tablet → YES ✓

beats.vo: Toaster… No! A toaster is not a computer — it only heats bread.
beats.caption: Toaster → NO ✗

beats.vo: Lamp… No! A lamp is not a computer.
beats.caption: Lamp → NO ✗

beats.vo: You are doing amazing. High five!
beats.caption: High five! You're amazing 🙌

beats.vo: One more thinking question — the same kind you will see later in your check.
beats.caption: Practice check question

beats.vo: Which one is a computer: a laptop, a lamp, or a bicycle bell?
beats.caption: Laptop · Lamp · Bicycle bell — which?

beats.vo: If you said laptop — you are right! Because it takes input, processes, and shows output.
beats.caption: Answer: Laptop ✓

beats.vo: A lamp and a bicycle bell are helpful, but they are not computers.
beats.caption: Lamp & bell → helpful, not computers

beats.vo: Let's lock it in. A computer has three jobs: input, process, and output.
beats.caption: Lock in: Input · Process · Output

beats.vo: Phone, laptop, tablet — computers. Toaster, lamp — not computers.
beats.caption: Computers vs not-computers

beats.vo: You learned Chapter one: What Is a Computer? Brilliant work today!
beats.caption: Chapter 1 complete · Brilliant!
